name: table
title: Table
summary: Presents data that has rows and columns — a price list, a comparison, a list of settings, a status of many things, the records a person works with — with named columns, optional row headers, a caption and footer rows; it scrolls in its own box when it does not fit; a column's header can ask for the rows in its order and rows can be chosen, while the table itself never sorts, filters, fetches or pages.

anatomy.description: The table's box: as wide as its layout gives it, as tall as its rows unless the layout limits it. It has no fill, edge or corner of its own. When the columns or the rows do not fit, it is the box they scroll in, and then the one part of the table that takes focus.
The name of the table, drawn above its first row at the start edge. It does not scroll sideways with the columns.
The first row: one header cell for each column. It can stay in view while the rows scroll under it.
The name of a column, in a label style and a quieter color than the data.
The whole header cell of a column that can be sorted, as one button: the column's name and its mark. It carries hover, focus and press, and asks the product for the rows in the column's order.
The glyph beside the name of a column that can be sorted: a two-way arrow while the rows are not in its order, an arrow up while they ascend by it, an arrow down while they descend.
One record: a cell for each column, as tall as its tallest cell.
The first cell of a row where the first column names its rows: the cell style at its emphasized weight. The first column can stay in view while the others scroll under it.
The cell before the first column of a table whose rows can be chosen: in a body row the row's checkbox, in the header row the checkbox for every row, in a footer row nothing.
One value: text that wraps inside its column, or a component of the product's (a tag, a link, inline code). It may be empty.

The one hairline between two rows, under the header row and above the footer rows, where rows are told apart by a line; also the line along the inner edge of a first column that stays in view, and along an edge of the box beyond which there is more to scroll to.
A quiet fill on every second body row.
The fill of a body row that is chosen, across its whole width, in place of a stripe.
A body row that stands for a record that has not arrived: as tall as a row of one line, holding what the product puts in its cells (a Skeleton), and no checkbox.
What stands in the place of the body rows of a table that has none: the product's own content (an Empty state), as wide as the table's box, under the header row.
A row after every body row that sums the columns up or notes something about them: the cell style at its emphasized weight.

One line under the last row, outside the columns: the product's sentence about what the table shows now (how many rows, how many chosen) at the start edge, and its pagination at the end edge. It does not scroll sideways with the columns.

props.name: caption
props.description: The name of the table, drawn above it ("Response times by region"). It is also what assistive technology calls the table and its scroll region. Prefer it to label wherever the page does not already name the table in sight.

props.name: label
props.description: The table's accessible name where no caption is drawn, because a heading just above it already says what it is. Not drawn. Ignored where caption is given.

props.name: density
props.description: How close the rows are. Regular (a 46 row in the default system) is for a table a person reads: a few rows, cells that wrap. Compact (a 32 row, smaller text) is for a table a person scans: hundreds of rows, identifiers and values. A design system may add values.

props.name: separation
props.description: How a row is told from the row next to it. divider: one hairline between them. gap: empty space and no line. Auto takes comp.table.separation, the design system's answer (divider in the default system).

props.name: striped
props.description: Fills every second body row with a quiet color, for a wide table of many similar rows where the eye loses its row on the way across. It can be combined with either separation.

props.name: rowHeaders
props.description: Says that the first column names its rows (a component, a region, a plan), so its cells are drawn and exposed as row headers. False for a table whose rows are named by no single column.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: Keeps the header row at the top of the table's box while its rows scroll under it. It has an effect only where the layout limits the table's height, so that the rows scroll in the table's own box.

props.name: stickyFirstColumn
props.description: Keeps the first column at the start edge while the other columns scroll sideways under it, for a wide table whose first column says what each row is. Released by itself where the column would take more than half of the box.

props.name: selection
props.description: Whether rows can be chosen. multiple puts a checkbox before the first column of every body row that has a value, and one in the header row that stands for all of them. none draws no such column and ignores a row's selected.

props.name: selectAllLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the checkbox in the header row that chooses every row ("Select all rows"). Not drawn. From the product's words where the instance gives none.

props.name: sortedAscendingLabel
props.description: What a platform that has no sort state of its own says after the name of the column the rows ascend by ("sorted ascending"). Not drawn. A platform that exposes the direction itself (the web) does not read it.

props.name: sortedDescendingLabel
props.description: What a platform that has no sort state of its own says after the name of the column the rows descend by ("sorted descending"). Not drawn. A platform that exposes the direction itself (the web) does not read it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Says that the product is fetching the rows — the first ones, another page of them, or the same ones in another order. The table is exposed as busy and draws the rows it is given meanwhile: the ones it had, or placeholder rows. It fetches nothing itself.

props.name: status
props.description: The product's sentence about what the table shows now ("1–20 of 132", "3 of 132 selected", "Loading"), drawn under the last row and told politely to assistive technology when it changes. The table counts nothing and writes no word of its own. Empty draws no status text.

items.name: column
items.summary: One column of the table: the text of its header cell, how its cells are aligned and wrapped, and whether its header asks for the rows in its order.

props.name: header
props.description: The text of the column's header cell ("Price"). Empty only where the table has no header row at all, and then for every column.

props.name: align
props.description: Where the content of the column's cells sits, header and footer cells included. start for text. end for numbers that are compared, so that their digits line up. center for a mark or a single word that is the same kind of answer in every row.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Whether the text of the column's cells may wrap. False keeps every cell on one line, for identifiers, dates, numbers and short values; the column is then as wide as its widest cell.

props.name: sortable
props.description: Says that the rows can be put in this column's order: its header cell is a button that asks for it. The table never orders rows itself. It needs a header: a sortable column without one is drawn as a plain column.

props.name: sort
props.description: The order the rows are in by this column, as the product has put them: the header draws it and exposes it. The product sets it after it has ordered its rows; one column at a time is not none.

props.name: value
props.description: The name the product knows the column by ("price"), carried by the sort event. Not drawn. Empty: the event carries the column's index alone.

items.name: row
items.summary: One row of the table: a cell for each column, in the order of the columns; a record that can be chosen where the table's selection says so.

props.name: footer
props.description: Says that the row is a footer row: drawn after every body row, in the emphasized weight, never striped. For sums, averages and notes about the columns.

props.name: value
props.description: The name the product knows the record by, carried by selectionChange. Not drawn. A body row without a value cannot be chosen: it has no checkbox.

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether the row is chosen. Read only while the table's selection is multiple and the row has a value.

props.name: selectLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the row's checkbox ("Select Islands"): words about this one record, so the instance's. Not drawn. Empty: the checkbox is named by the row's header cell where rowHeaders is true.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Says that the row stands for a record that has not arrived. It is drawn as a body row at least one line tall, holds what the product puts in its cells (a Skeleton) or nothing, has no checkbox and is hidden from assistive technology.

items.name: cell
items.summary: One value of a row: plain text, a component of the product's, or nothing.

slots.name: content
slots.description: What the cell holds in place of plain text: a tag, a link, inline code, a button, a picture, any view of the product's. The table places it and styles nothing inside it (TBL-15).

items.name: tag
items.summary: A tag placed in a cell: the Tag component, as it is drawn anywhere else.

props.name: label
props.description: The tag's text.

props.name: variant
props.description: The tag's look.

props.name: status
props.description: What the tag reports.

props.name: size
props.description: The tag's size; small in a table cell, so that it does not make its row taller.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: What the table draws in the place of its body rows while it has none and is not loading: the product's Empty state, or its own sentence. The table gives it the box's width and room above and below, and does nothing else to it. A fixture's string is drawn as plain text in its place.

slots.name: pagination
slots.description: What stands at the end edge of the status line: the product's Pagination, or its own controls for the part of the rows that is shown. The table places it and does nothing else to it. A fixture's string is drawn as plain text in its place.

events.name: sort
events.description: The user pressed the header of a sortable column; carries column (the column's value), index (its place among the columns of data, from 0) and direction (ascending or descending: the one asked for, TBL-34). The table changes nothing: the product orders its rows and sets the column's sort.

events.name: selectionChange
events.description: The user changed which rows are chosen, by a row's checkbox or by the one for every row; carries values: the values of the chosen rows after the change, in row order.

behavior.text: THE table SHALL draw, from top to bottom, its caption where it has one, one header row holding one header cell for each column, its body rows in the order given, and its footer rows after every body row, each row holding one cell for each column in the order of the columns; THE table SHALL be at least as wide as the layout gives it, SHALL draw no fill, no edge, no corner and no elevation of its own around its rows, and SHALL bring no outer space of its own, so that it is spaced by what holds it.

THE table SHALL size every column from its content: a column SHALL never be narrower than the widest thing in it that cannot break — a word, a number, a cell of a column whose wrap is false, a component — with the cell's inline paddings; WHILE the columns at those least widths fit the table's box THE table SHALL share the box's width among them in proportion to their content, so that the table fills its box and a column of long text takes what the short columns leave; THE table SHALL NOT give a column a width in a unit of its own, and a width the product gives a column SHALL replace what the content would give it.
behavior.verify: The fixture long-cells: the three columns whose wrap is false are as wide as their widest cell, and the Description column takes the rest and wraps.

behavior.text: THE table SHALL wrap the text of a cell inside its column, breaking lines by the rules of the text's language, and SHALL never cut it or end it with an ellipsis; a run with no break opportunity (an identifier, an address) SHALL NOT be broken inside and widens its column instead (TBL-2, TBL-17); WHERE a column's wrap is false THE table SHALL keep every cell of that column, its header cell included, on one line.

THE table SHALL pad every cell at the top and bottom by comp.table.cell.padding-block.regular and at the start and end by comp.table.cell.padding-inline.regular while density is regular, and by comp.table.cell.padding-block.compact and comp.table.cell.padding-inline.compact while density is compact, the first and the last cell of a row included; SHALL set a cell's text in comp.table.cell.text.typescale.regular or comp.table.cell.text.typescale.compact by density, in comp.table.cell.text.color, with digits in figures of equal width so that the numbers of a column line up; SHALL make a row as tall as its tallest cell and no taller, with no height of its own; and SHALL align the cells of a row to the top, so that the first lines of a row share a baseline.
behavior.verify: Under the default system a regular row of one-line cells is 46 high (12 + 22 + 12) and a compact one 32 (6 + 20 + 6).

behavior.text: THE table SHALL set a column's header cell in comp.table.header.text.typescale.regular or comp.table.header.text.typescale.compact by density, in comp.table.header.text.color, with the paddings of a cell (TBL-4), and SHALL fill the header row with comp.table.header.container.color; the header cells of a row SHALL align to the bottom, so that the last line of each sits next to the data it names. IF every column's header is empty THE table SHALL draw no header row and no line for it, and the table then relies on its row headers (TBL-6).
behavior.verify: The fixture no-header gives two columns with empty headers and rowHeaders true: no header row is drawn and each row's first cell is its header.

behavior.text: WHILE rowHeaders is true THE table SHALL treat the first cell of every body row and of every footer row as the header of its row: it SHALL draw that cell in the cell's text style at its emphasized weight — the style's weight plus sys.typescale.emphasis.body — in comp.table.cell.text.color, with a cell's paddings and no fill of its own, and SHALL expose it as a row header (TBL-24); WHILE rowHeaders is false THE table SHALL draw and expose the first column as cells, except that a first cell the product's own content already marks as the header of its row (on the web a th whose scope is row) SHALL be drawn and exposed as one whatever rowHeaders says: rowHeaders adds row headers and takes none away. WHILE selection is multiple the first column is the first column of data, after the selection column (TBL-42).

THE table SHALL align the content of every cell of a column, its header cell and its footer cells included, as the column's align names — start: at the start edge of the cell; end: at the end edge, for numbers that are compared digit by digit; center: in the middle, for a mark or a single word that is the same kind of answer in every row — and SHALL align every line of a wrapped cell the same way; a value of align the table does not define SHALL be treated as start.

WHILE the table's separation is divider (TBL-9) THE table SHALL draw one line of comp.table.divider.thickness in comp.table.divider.color across its whole width under the header row, between every two rows that follow each other, and between the last body row and the first footer row, without adding to a row's height or moving its content; it SHALL draw no line above the first row or below the last, and no line between columns.

THE table SHALL tell a row from the row next to it as its separation names: WHILE separation is auto, as comp.table.separation names, which follows sys.behavior.separation unless a design system sets it apart; WHILE separation is divider or gap, as that value names, whatever the tokens say; divider draws the lines of TBL-8 and gap leaves the space of TBL-10. WHEN separation, or the token it follows, changes THE table SHALL draw the other form at once, without animation, keeping its scroll position; WHEN separation names a value the table does not define THE table SHALL treat it as auto and in debug builds report the unknown value. A platform that cannot draw a choice SHALL fall back to the first value, divider, and state that in its README.

WHILE the table's separation is gap (TBL-9) THE table SHALL leave comp.table.row.gap of empty space under the header row, between every two rows that follow each other, and between the last body row and the first footer row, SHALL draw none of the lines of TBL-8, and SHALL leave no such space above the first row or below the last; the rows SHALL stay exposed as rows (TBL-24).

WHILE striped is true THE table SHALL fill every second body row — the second, the fourth and so on, counted among the body rows as they are shown — with comp.table.stripe.container.color across the row's whole width, paddings included, and SHALL fill neither the header row nor a footer row with it; the fill SHALL change nothing else about the row, and the row separation of TBL-9 SHALL be drawn as without it.

WHERE caption is not empty THE table SHALL draw it above the header row, at the start edge of the table's box, in comp.table.caption.text.typescale and comp.table.caption.text.color, wrapping inside the box's width, comp.table.caption.gap above the first row; the caption SHALL stay where it is while the columns scroll sideways (TBL-17) and SHALL be the table's accessible name (TBL-23).

WHERE a row's footer is true THE table SHALL draw it after every body row, in the order given, as a footer row: its cells in the cell's text style at its emphasized weight — the style's weight plus sys.typescale.emphasis.body — in comp.table.cell.text.color, aligned as their columns are, never striped, and exposed as rows of the table that follow its body; IF a row whose footer is false is given after a footer row THE table SHALL still draw every body row before every footer row and in debug builds report the order.
behavior.verify: The fixture totals ends with a row of sums whose footer is true.

behavior.text: WHERE a cell has no content THE table SHALL draw nothing in it, keep its place and its paddings so that the cells after it stay in their columns, and expose it as an empty cell; THE table SHALL NOT put a dash, a word or any other mark of its own in it. IF a row holds fewer cells than the table has columns THE table SHALL keep the row's place and its height and leave the places of the missing cells empty at the row's end: a platform that builds its rows SHALL draw them as empty cells, and a platform that draws the product's own rows (the web) SHALL write no cell into them, so that there the row's line and a stripe end at its last cell, and in debug builds SHALL report the row; IF it holds more THE table SHALL draw only as many as it has columns and in debug builds report the row.

WHERE a cell holds a component or any content of the product's that is not plain text — a tag, a link, inline code, a button, a picture — THE table SHALL place it by the column's alignment (TBL-7) on the cell's first line, SHALL add nothing to it and style nothing inside it, and SHALL let pointer, touch and keyboard input reach it as it would outside the table, in the reading order of the cells.
behavior.verify: The fixture tags holds a small tag in each platform's cell: each is drawn as the tag's own spec says, centred on the first line of its cell, and adds no height to the row.

behavior.text: THE table, its rows and its cells SHALL NOT take pointer, touch or keyboard input of their own and SHALL NOT change anything they draw under a pointer, a press or focus: a row has no hovered, focused or pressed state and is not pressed as a whole, and a cell is not a stop in the focus order. Three parts of the table take input, each by its own sentences: the header cell of a sortable column, which is a button (TBL-32 to TBL-41); the checkboxes of a table whose selection is multiple, which are the Checkbox component (TBL-42 to TBL-47); and the scroll region while the table scrolls (TBL-22). WHILE no column is sortable and selection is none THE table SHALL emit no event.

WHEN the columns at their least widths (TBL-2) are wider than the table's box THE table SHALL keep its box at the width the layout gives it and scroll its columns sideways inside that box, header row, body rows and footer rows together, beginning at the start edge; it SHALL never be wider than its layout and SHALL never make what holds it scroll sideways; a wheel, a trackpad, a drag on a touch screen and the keys of TBL-22 SHALL scroll it.
behavior.verify: The fixture wide holds nine columns that do not wrap and is wider than any harness's stage: the stage does not scroll, the table's box does.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout gives the table less height than its rows need THE table SHALL scroll its rows up and down inside its own box, the caption above them as the first thing in the box, where it MAY scroll away with the rows on a platform whose caption is part of what scrolls (the web's native caption), and the status line staying at the bottom of the box (TBL-51); WHERE the layout sets no such limit THE table SHALL be exactly as tall as its caption and its rows, and SHALL set no height and no number of rows of its own.

WHILE stickyHeader is true and the table scrolls its rows in its own box (TBL-18) THE table SHALL keep the header row at the top of that box while the rows pass under it, filled with comp.table.sticky.container.color under comp.table.header.container.color so that nothing shows through it, and SHALL draw a line of comp.table.divider.thickness in comp.table.divider.color under it whatever the separation is while a row is under it; WHILE stickyHeader is false, or the table does not scroll its rows in its own box, THE header row SHALL scroll with the rows.
behavior.verify: The fixture sticky-header needs a box shorter than its twelve rows; a harness whose stage sets no height draws it whole, and the test of this requirement sets the height itself.

behavior.text: WHILE stickyFirstColumn is true and the table scrolls sideways (TBL-17) THE table SHALL keep the first column — its header cell, its cells and its footer cells — at the start edge of the box while the other columns pass under it, each of its cells filled with comp.table.sticky.container.color under the fill its row gives it (comp.table.header.container.color in the header row, comp.table.stripe.container.color in a striped row), and SHALL draw a line of comp.table.divider.thickness in comp.table.divider.color along its inner edge for the table's whole height while a column is under it; WHILE both stickyHeader and stickyFirstColumn hold THE first header cell SHALL stay above both. IF the first column is wider than half of the table's box THE table SHALL let it scroll with the other columns, so that a narrow window is never filled by the column that stays.
behavior.verify: The fixture wide-sticky-column: after scrolling to the end, the Region column is still at the start edge with a line along its inner edge. At a stage narrower than twice the Region column, the column scrolls away with the others.

behavior.text: WHILE the table scrolls sideways and columns lie beyond an inline edge of its box THE table SHALL draw a line of comp.table.divider.thickness in comp.table.divider.color along that edge of the box for the table's whole height, and SHALL remove it when the scroll reaches that edge; at the start edge of a table whose first column is kept in view the line of TBL-20 is that line. THE table SHALL show that there is more with these lines alone: no shadow, no fade and no color that is not the divider's.

WHILE the table scrolls in its own box, sideways or up and down, THE table SHALL make that box one stop in the focus order, before anything in its cells that takes focus, exposed as a region that carries the table's name (TBL-23); WHILE it has keyboard focus the box SHALL draw the system's focus indicator inside its edge — sys.focus.outer-width wide in the color role focus-ring, set in from the edge by sys.focus.offset so that nothing clips it, and never animated — and the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End SHALL scroll it as the platform scrolls a region, the left and right arrow keys moving the view left and right in either layout direction; WHILE the table does not scroll THE table SHALL NOT be a stop in the focus order and SHALL expose no region.
behavior.verify: Test the fixture wide at a stage narrower than its columns (one Tab reaches the box; the right arrow key scrolls it) and the fixture basic (Tab passes the table).

behavior.text: THE table SHALL take its accessible name from caption where caption is not empty, and from label otherwise, and SHALL NOT draw label; IF both are empty THE table SHALL be exposed without a name and in debug builds report that a table has no name, and WHILE such a table scrolls in its own box that box SHALL still be a stop in the focus order (TBL-22), exposed as a region without a name, because the keyboard must be able to scroll it; IF both are given THE caption SHALL be the name and label SHALL be ignored.

THE table SHALL be exposed to assistive technology as a table with its number of rows and columns, its header cells as column headers, its first cells as row headers while rowHeaders is true, and every cell associated with the header of its column and, where there is one, of its row, so that a person moving cell by cell hears what each value belongs to; a platform that has no table semantics SHALL expose each row as one group in reading order and each cell with its column header before its own content. Keeping a header row or a first column in view, striping, the density and scrolling SHALL change nothing that is exposed.
behavior.verify: On the web: the accessibility tree of every fixture has the roles table, row, columnheader, rowheader and cell, also while the table scrolls in its own box and while a column is kept in view.

behavior.text: WHEN the table's rows, columns or cells change THE table SHALL draw the new content at once, without a motion, keeping its scroll position where the content it showed still exists, and SHALL NOT announce the change by itself. The one place where the table tells a change is its status line, and what that says is the product's (TBL-52); WHEN rows are replaced because the product ordered or fetched them THE table SHALL keep keyboard focus on the sort button or the checkbox that had it, where that control still exists.

THE table SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the table is shown THE table SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its content and the column a person was looking at in view.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE table SHALL lay its columns out from the right, the first column at the right edge; SHALL apply paddings and the alignments start and end by the layout direction; SHALL begin its sideways scroll at the right edge; SHALL keep a first column that stays in view (TBL-20) at the right edge with its line on its left; and SHALL draw the lines of TBL-21 at the edges beyond which columns lie. Top and bottom SHALL NOT change: the header row is the first row and the footer rows the last in either direction.
behavior.verify: The fixture rtl-wide-sticky-column: the first column is at the right edge, the table opens showing it, and scrolling moves the other columns under it from the left.

behavior.text: THE table SHALL lay out the text of each cell, of each header cell and of the caption as text of its own direction, isolated from the cells beside it: it takes the base direction of its first strong character, or the layout direction where it has none, so that a left-to-right name, an identifier, a number with its sign, unit or currency, a version and a date keep their own order in a right-to-left layout; THE table SHALL place that text by the column's alignment in the layout direction, not by the text's own, and SHALL NOT reverse the digits of a number: a column of numbers whose align is end is at the left edge of its cells in a right-to-left layout, with its digits written left to right.
behavior.verify: The fixture rtl holds Arabic headers and decimal numbers in end-aligned columns: the numbers end at the left edge of their cells and read 18.50, not 05.81. The fixture ltr-cells-rtl holds left-to-right names in a right-to-left layout: each keeps its order and starts at the right edge of its cell.

behavior.text: WHILE the text size is enlarged THE table SHALL grow every text style with it, give up none of its paddings and none of its lines (they MAY grow with the text where the design system's units follow the text size), size its columns again from the larger content (TBL-2), wrap what can wrap and scroll in its own box where the columns no longer fit (TBL-17); it SHALL cut no content, SHALL set no fixed height on a row or a cell, SHALL lose no content when the reader raises line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing or word spacing, and SHALL need no sideways scrolling of what holds it at a width of 320 points.
behavior.verify: On the web at 200 % text and at a 320 wide window: every fixture's text is whole, and only the table's own box scrolls sideways.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors (the web's forced-colors mode, and a platform's equivalent where it has one) THE table SHALL draw every line of TBL-8, TBL-19, TBL-20 and TBL-21 in the platform's text color and its text in that color, SHALL keep header cells, row headers and footer cells told apart by their text styles, and, because the mode removes fills, SHALL draw the lines of TBL-8 in a striped table whatever its separation is, so that its rows are still told apart.
behavior.verify: On the web, with forced colors emulated: the fixture separation-gap-striped draws a CanvasText line between its rows; no fixture relies on a background color.

behavior.text: WHEN density names a value that the active design system does not have THE table SHALL render with the default value's tokens, and in debug builds report the unknown value.

WHERE a column's sortable is true and its header is not empty THE table SHALL draw that column's header cell as one button, the sort button: its container is the whole box of the header cell, paddings included, with square corners; it holds the column's header as its label, in the header's text style (TBL-5), and the sort mark — one glyph of the system's icon set in a box of comp.table.header.icon.size, drawn through the icon helper with sys.icon.family.unselected, sys.icon.fill.unselected, the weight comp.table.header.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max — comp.table.header.gap after the label's box, at the height of the label's last line, so that a header that wraps keeps its mark at the edge of its label rather than after the last word; in a column whose align is end the mark SHALL stand before the label, so that the end of the label stays on the edge its numbers end at. The mark's box SHALL be kept whatever the column's sort is, so that a change of order moves no label and changes no column's width. IF sortable is true and header is empty THE table SHALL draw the column as one that is not sortable and in debug builds report it.
behavior.verify: The fixture sortable: three sort buttons, each as large as its header cell. The fixture sorted-end: in the two end-aligned columns the mark is before the label and the labels end where the numbers end.

behavior.text: THE table SHALL draw the order the product sets and never make one: WHILE a sortable column's sort is none its sort button is the part sort — the label in comp.table.sort.label.color, the glyph swap_vert in comp.table.sort.icon.color, the container in comp.table.sort.container.color; WHILE its sort is ascending or descending it is the part sorted — the label in comp.table.sorted.label.color, the glyph arrow_upward for ascending and arrow_downward for descending in comp.table.sorted.icon.color, the container in comp.table.sorted.container.color. THE table SHALL NOT reorder, compare, filter or hide a row, SHALL NOT change a column's sort itself, and SHALL draw its rows in the order it is given whatever any sort says. WHEN a column's sort changes THE table SHALL draw the other glyph and colors at once, with no motion but that of a state change (TBL-35). IF more than one column's sort is not none THE table SHALL draw each as it is given and in debug builds report it: the rows have one order. A sort on a column whose sortable is false SHALL be ignored.
behavior.verify: The fixture sortable: Name is sorted ascending (arrow_upward, the label in the color of the data); the two other headers show swap_vert in the header's color. The rows are in the order the fixture gives them.

behavior.text: WHEN the user activates a sort button by pointer, touch, Enter or Space THE table SHALL emit sort exactly once, carrying the column's value, its index among the columns of data and the direction asked for — ascending WHILE the column's sort is none or descending, descending WHILE it is ascending — and SHALL change nothing it draws but the answer to the press: the mark, the colors and the rows stay as they are until the product sets sort and gives the rows in their new order. The direction is what the person asked; the product MAY set another, or none. THE table SHALL keep keyboard focus on the sort button through the press and through the change of rows that follows it. WHERE the product gave the control a destination in place of an action (on the web an anchor in the header cell, whose address is the same table in the other order) THE table SHALL emit sort once and then let the platform follow the destination unless the product cancelled the event, and Space SHALL NOT activate it, as it activates no link.
behavior.verify: Press Name in the fixture sortable (sorted ascending): one sort event with direction descending; the mark is still arrow_upward until the test sets sort.

behavior.text: WHILE a sort button is hovered, keyboard-focused or pressed THE table SHALL render its container, its label, its mark and its opacity from the component tokens of its part (sort or sorted) in the highest-precedence active state, with precedence pressed over focused over hovered; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT select the focused state. A change between states SHALL take comp.table.motion.state-duration with comp.table.motion.state-easing and SHALL be immediate where motion is reduced. The state layer SHALL cover the header cell and nothing beside it, and WHILE the header row or the column is kept in view (TBL-19, TBL-20) SHALL be drawn over comp.table.sticky.container.color, so that nothing shows through it.

WHEN a sort button receives keyboard focus THE table SHALL show the system's focus indicator inside the edge of its header cell without animation — sys.focus.outer-width wide in the color role focus-ring, set in from the edge by sys.focus.offset so that neither the next cell, the box's edge nor a header kept in view clips it, with the inner stroke of sys.focus.inner-width where the system has one; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT show it. WHEN keyboard focus moves to a sort button or a checkbox that is under a header row, a first column or a status line kept in view, or outside the box, THE table SHALL scroll its box so that the whole control is in view beside them.

WHEN a sort button is pressed by pointer, touch, Enter or Space THE table SHALL show the pressed state without delay and SHALL keep it visible for at least sys.motion.duration.press-hold, even when the press ends sooner.

WHILE a sort button is pressed THE table SHALL answer as sys.behavior.pressed-feedback names: overlay applies the pressed tokens to the whole container at once; ripple grows the pressed state layer from the point of contact (from the center for keyboard activation); dim applies the pressed opacity to the whole control and draws no state layer; none draws no answer to the press. Under ripple and dim only the container color stays with the state under the press; label, mark and opacity still come from the pressed tokens. Under none every part stays with the state under the press. The ripple grows over comp.table.motion.feedback-duration with comp.table.motion.state-easing, fades over comp.table.motion.state-duration with comp.table.motion.state-easing once the press has ended and press-hold has passed, and appears whole where motion is reduced.

THE table SHALL show the keyboard focus of a sort button as sys.behavior.focus-style names (ring or glow); a platform that cannot draw a choice SHALL fall back to the first value and state that in its README. A sort button's container has square corners, the header cell's, so sys.shape.corner-smoothing has nothing to ease on it.

THE table SHALL make a sort button's hit area its whole header cell, with no gap to the hit area of the header cell beside it. WHERE input is touch, or the platform cannot tell the input type, a header row that holds a sort button SHALL be at least sys.target.touch high, drawn so, at both densities, because a header cell cannot extend a hit area over the row under it; for a fine pointer it SHALL be at least sys.target.pointer high WHILE density is regular, and WHILE density is compact as high as its density gives. A header cell narrower than the target SHALL extend its hit area along the row no further than halfway into the paddings between it and the cell beside it.
behavior.verify: On the web with a coarse pointer emulated, the fixture sortable-compact: the header row is 48 high. With a fine pointer it is 32.

behavior.text: THE table SHALL expose a sortable column's header cell as the column header it is (TBL-24) with the order its sort names — ascending, descending, or none for a column that can be sorted and is not — and the sort button inside it as a button named by the column's header; the sort mark SHALL be hidden from assistive technology. On the web these are aria-sort on the header cell and the product's own button in it. WHERE a platform has no sort state THE table SHALL say the order after the button's name with sortedAscendingLabel or sortedDescendingLabel, which come from the instance or from the product's words under the keys of the same names and from nowhere else; IF such a platform is given neither, THE table SHALL expose the button by its name alone and in debug builds report the missing word once. THE table SHALL NOT announce an order itself when it changes: the header cell's state says it, and a product that wants it spoken writes it in status (TBL-52).
behavior.verify: On the web: the accessibility tree of the fixture sortable has three column headers with aria-sort ascending, none and none, each holding a button; the fixture basic has no aria-sort.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple THE table SHALL draw a selection column before its first column: in the header row a cell holding the checkbox for every row (TBL-45), in each body row that has a value a cell holding that row's checkbox, and an empty cell in a body row without a value, in a placeholder row and in a footer row. Each checkbox is the Checkbox component as its own spec draws it, with no label drawn, placed on the cell's first line (TBL-15) with the edge of its box, not of its round container, at the cell's padding, so that the boxes stand on the line the text of the other cells starts at: the selection cell's paddings are a cell's paddings less half of what comp.checkbox.container.size exceeds comp.checkbox.box.size by (never less than 0), the round container reaching into them, and the column is as wide as the checkbox's container and those paddings. The selection column is not a column of data: it has no header text, the first column of rowHeaders and of stickyFirstColumn is the one after it, and a sort event's index does not count it. WHILE stickyFirstColumn is true the selection column SHALL stay in view with the first column (TBL-20), and the two together are what is released when they would take more than half of the box. WHILE selection is none THE table SHALL draw no such column and no checkbox, SHALL ignore every row's selected, and SHALL emit no selectionChange.
behavior.verify: The fixture selection: five cells in each row for four columns of data; the footer row's first cell is empty; in the default system each checkbox's box starts 16 from the cell's start edge, where the text of a cell starts, and the column is 18 + 2 × 16 = 50 wide. The fixture selection-sticky-column: scrolled to the end, the checkbox and the Region column are both at the start edge.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is multiple and a body row's selected is true THE table SHALL draw that row as chosen: comp.table.row.selected.container.color across its whole width, paddings and the selection cell included, in place of the stripe of TBL-11 where the row would have one; the text of its cells and of its row header in comp.table.row.selected.text.color; and its checkbox checked. What a cell holds that is not plain text SHALL keep its own colors (TBL-15). In a column kept in view the fill SHALL lie over comp.table.sticky.container.color. The lines and the gap between rows (TBL-8, TBL-10) SHALL be drawn as without it. The fill SHALL change at once, without a motion of the table's own. A footer row and a placeholder row are never chosen.
behavior.verify: The fixture selection-striped: the second row is selected and takes the selected fill, not the stripe; the fourth keeps its stripe.

behavior.text: WHEN the user changes a row's checkbox — by a press, or by Space while it has focus — THE table SHALL set that row's selected to the checkbox's new state and emit selectionChange exactly once, carrying the values of every chosen row after the change in row order. A press on the row outside its checkbox's hit area SHALL choose nothing (TBL-16). WHEN the product sets a row's selected THE table SHALL draw it and SHALL NOT emit. THE table SHALL keep which rows are chosen by their values: WHEN rows are given again in another order (TBL-33) each row SHALL be drawn chosen or not by its own selected, and the table SHALL carry no selection over to a row it is not given.

WHILE selection is multiple THE table SHALL keep the checkbox for every row in step with the body rows it holds that have a value: checked WHILE each of them is chosen, in its mixed (indeterminate) state WHILE some are and some are not, unchecked WHILE none is, and disabled WHILE there is no such row. WHEN the user activates it while it is unchecked or mixed THE table SHALL choose every such row, and while it is checked SHALL clear every one, and SHALL emit selectionChange exactly once with the values after the change. "Every row" is every row the table has been given: it SHALL NOT claim to choose records the product has not given it (the rows of other pages), and a product that offers that says so with a control of its own.
behavior.verify: The fixtures selection (two of four chosen: mixed), selection-all (checked) and selection-compact (none chosen: unchecked); the fixture empty-selection (no rows: disabled).

behavior.text: THE table SHALL name each row's checkbox by that row's selectLabel; WHERE selectLabel is empty and rowHeaders is true the checkbox SHALL be named by the text of the row's header cell; IF it has neither THE table SHALL expose the checkbox without a name and in debug builds report the row once per table. THE table SHALL name the checkbox for every row by selectAllLabel, from the instance or from the product's words under the key selectAllLabel and from nowhere else; IF neither gives it THE table SHALL still draw the checkbox, expose it without a name and in debug builds report the missing word. A table whose selection is multiple SHALL still be exposed as a table (TBL-24), its rows as rows and its selection cells as cells: which rows are chosen is said by the checked state of their checkboxes, the header checkbox says checked, mixed or not checked, and the table SHALL add no selected state to a row and no role of a grid.
behavior.verify: On the web: the accessibility tree of the fixture selection has the roles table, row, columnheader, rowheader, cell and checkbox, no grid and no aria-selected; the header checkbox is mixed.

behavior.text: THE table SHALL make each sort button and each checkbox its own stop in the focus order, in reading order — the scroll region first while the table scrolls (TBL-22), then the header row's controls from the start, then each row's checkbox followed by whatever in that row's cells takes focus — and SHALL handle no key that moves focus from cell to cell: the arrow keys scroll the region or do what the focused control does with them. A checkbox's hit area SHALL be its whole selection cell, in width and in height. WHERE input is touch, or the platform cannot tell the input type, a row that holds a checkbox SHALL be at least sys.target.touch high, drawn so, at both densities, and its selection cell at least sys.target.touch wide; for a fine pointer the row SHALL be at least sys.target.pointer high WHILE density is regular, and WHILE density is compact as high as its density gives.
behavior.verify: Test the fixture sortable-selection: Tab visits Name, Stock, Price, then each row's checkbox in turn; the arrow keys move focus nowhere.

behavior.text: WHILE the table has no body row, loading is false and the empty slot has content THE table SHALL draw that content in the place of the body rows: under the header row and its line, before any footer row, as wide as the table's box and staying in view while the columns scroll sideways, with comp.table.empty.padding-block above and below it and a cell's inline padding at its sides (TBL-4), with no line, no stripe and no fill of the table's through it. THE table SHALL expose it as one row holding one cell that spans every column, SHALL add no word, glyph or role of its own to it, and SHALL NOT announce it (TBL-25): where a search or a filter emptied the table, the product's Empty state is the live one. WHILE the table has no body row and the empty slot has no content THE table SHALL draw its caption, its header row and its footer rows and nothing between them. WHILE the table has a body row THE table SHALL NOT draw the empty slot's content.
behavior.verify: The fixture empty: the header row, then the slot's text across the box. On the web its accessibility tree has two rows, the second with one cell.

behavior.text: WHILE loading is true THE table SHALL be exposed as busy; SHALL draw the rows it is given as they are — the rows it had, or placeholder rows (TBL-50) — and SHALL NOT draw the empty slot's content, even with no body row; SHALL keep its header row, its sort buttons, its checkboxes and its status line working as without it; SHALL change no color, no opacity and no size of its own because of it; and SHALL announce nothing itself when loading begins or ends: the product says it in status (TBL-52). THE table SHALL fetch nothing, wait for nothing and time nothing: loading is true for as long as the product says so.
behavior.verify: The fixture loading: the four rows it had, drawn as in the fixture selection, and on the web aria-busy on the table.

behavior.text: WHERE a row's placeholder is true THE table SHALL draw it as a body row — counted for stripes, parted from its neighbours as TBL-9 says, with a cell's paddings — at least as tall as a body row holding one line of text at the table's density, however little its cells hold; SHALL place in each cell what the product gives it there (a Skeleton, by TBL-15) or nothing; SHALL draw no checkbox in its selection cell and count it neither as a body row for the header checkbox (TBL-45) nor as a row for the empty slot (TBL-48); and SHALL hide the row from assistive technology, so that a person hears that the table is busy and not a row of nothing. IF a row's placeholder is true while loading is false THE table SHALL draw it all the same and in debug builds report it.
behavior.verify: The fixture loading-placeholders: five rows of empty cells, each 46 high under the default system, no checkbox in any of them, and the header checkbox disabled.

behavior.text: WHERE status is not empty or the pagination slot has content THE table SHALL draw a status line under its last row: the status text at the start edge in comp.table.status.text.typescale and comp.table.status.text.color, the pagination slot's content at the end edge, both centered on the line's height, with comp.table.status.padding-block above and below, a cell's inline padding at its sides (TBL-4) and at least comp.table.status.gap between the two; WHERE the two do not fit on one line THE table SHALL put the status text above the pagination, comp.table.status.gap apart, each at the start edge, and the text SHALL wrap and never be cut. The status line SHALL be as wide as the table's box and SHALL stay where it is while the columns scroll sideways (TBL-17). WHILE separation is divider THE table SHALL draw one line of comp.table.divider.thickness in comp.table.divider.color above it. WHILE the table scrolls its rows in its own box (TBL-18) the status line SHALL stay at the bottom of that box while the rows pass under it, filled with comp.table.sticky.container.color, with that line above it whatever the separation is while a row is under it. WHERE status is empty and the slot has no content THE table SHALL draw no status line and leave no room for one.
behavior.verify: The fixture status-pagination. The fixture data needs a box shorter than its rows for the line to stay; the test of this requirement sets the height itself.

behavior.text: THE table SHALL expose the status text as a status that assistive technology is told of politely WHEN it changes, without moving focus, and SHALL tell it nothing when the text is first drawn with the table. THE table SHALL write no word into it and SHALL count nothing for it: how many rows there are, which of them are shown and how many are chosen are the product's to say, in its own language. THE table SHALL place the content of the pagination slot and SHALL NOT style it, give it keys or listen to it: the table shows the rows it is given, emits nothing about pages, and holds no page number and no page size.
behavior.verify: Set status on the fixture status after the first render: one polite announcement of the new text.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE table SHALL draw the selection column at the right edge, before the first column; SHALL place a sort mark after its label on the left, and before it — on the right — in a column whose align is end; SHALL draw the status text at the right edge of the status line and the pagination at the left; and SHALL keep the selection column and a first column that stay in view at the right (TBL-27). The glyphs swap_vert, arrow_upward and arrow_downward show an order and not a direction of reading, and SHALL NOT be mirrored. The status text SHALL be laid out as text of its own direction (TBL-28).
behavior.verify: The fixture rtl-sortable-selection.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors THE table SHALL draw a sort button's label and mark in the platform's button-text color and its focus indicator in the platform's highlight color, SHALL keep the sorted column told from the others by its glyph alone, and, because the mode removes the fill of a chosen row, SHALL rely on the row's checkbox, which the Checkbox draws checked in that mode, to say that the row is chosen; it SHALL draw the line above a status line kept in view in the platform's text color (TBL-30).
behavior.verify: On the web, with forced colors emulated: in the fixture selection a chosen row and one that is not differ by their checkboxes; no fixture relies on a background color.

behavior.text: WHILE the text size is enlarged THE table SHALL grow a sort button's label and its mark's box with it, wrap the label inside its column where the column's wrap allows it and keep the mark on the label's last line, grow the status text and wrap it, keep the selection column as wide as its checkbox and paddings, and lay the status line out in two lines where one no longer fits (TBL-51); nothing of these SHALL be cut, and TBL-29 holds for a table with every one of them at a width of 320 points.
behavior.verify: On the web at 200 % text and at a 320 wide window, the fixtures sortable-long-headers and data: every header label is whole and only the table's own box scrolls sideways.

behavior.text: WHILE the system's icon set cannot yet draw a sort mark (its font is still loading) THE table SHALL draw nothing in the mark's box, never the glyph's name as text, SHALL keep the box, and SHALL draw the glyph once the set can; the sort button SHALL work all the same.

WHERE the platform draws the product's own elements and script does not run (the web) THE table SHALL still draw, from the product's markup alone, everything of TBL-32, TBL-33, TBL-42, TBL-43, TBL-48, TBL-50 and TBL-51 that is drawing: a sort button and the mark of the order the header cell names, the hover, focus and press of the button, the selection column, a chosen row, the empty content, placeholder rows and the status line; a sort button that is an anchor and checkboxes that are the platform's own inside the product's form SHALL work as the platform makes them work. What needs script and is then absent: the events, the header checkbox kept in step and choosing every row (TBL-45), the busy state where the product did not write it, keeping focus through a change of rows, and what TBL-22 already loses. Nothing SHALL be hidden that script would have to reveal.
behavior.verify: On the web with scripting off: the fixtures sortable, selection, empty, loading-placeholders and status-pagination, written as the README writes them, are drawn as with it.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the table's box while the table scrolls in it; then to each sortable column's header button, in reading order; then, row by row, to the row's checkbox where rows can be chosen and to whatever in its cells takes focus. A table that does not scroll, sorts nothing and selects nothing is not a stop.
On a sortable column's header: asks for the rows in that column's order — ascending, or descending where they already ascend by it. Where the header is a link, Enter alone.
On a row's checkbox: chooses the row or lets it go. On the header row's checkbox: chooses every row, or lets every row go where all are chosen.
While the box has focus: scroll it. Left and right move the view left and right in either layout direction.

keyboard.keys: Page Up / Page Down, Home / End
keyboard.action: While the box has focus: scroll it by a page, or to its beginning or end, as the platform scrolls a region.

accessibility.labeling: The table is named by its caption, or by label where no caption is drawn (TBL-23). Header cells name their columns and, while rowHeaders is true, first cells name their rows; every cell is associated with both (TBL-24). While the table scrolls in its own box, that box is a region with the same name, so that a person who reaches it by keyboard hears what scrolls. A sortable column's button is named by the column's header, and the header cell carries the order (TBL-41). A row's checkbox is named by selectLabel, or by the row's header; the header row's by selectAllLabel (TBL-46). The status line is the product's sentence, told politely when it changes (TBL-52).
notes: The table, its rows and its cells take no input (TBL-16). What does — a sortable column's header, the checkboxes, the scroll box — is a control or a region: a header's hit area is its whole cell and a checkbox's its whole selection cell, each at least the touch target high for touch at both densities (TBL-40, TBL-47); the compact density is lower than the pointer target, as a compact tree row is. What is pressable inside a cell (a link, a button) meets the minimum target by its own spec.

A table is for data that has rows and columns. Do not use it to place things side by side: assistive technology announces rows, columns and headers for every cell, which is noise around content that is not tabular. Use the layout.

Give every table a name (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2): a caption that everyone sees is best; label is for a table whose heading already names it. A table that scrolls and has no name is a focus stop a person cannot tell from any other, so debug builds report it (TBL-23).

Header cells are structure, not style (WCAG 1.3.1). Every column has a header cell unless the table has no header row at all; rowHeaders is true whenever the first column says what each row is. A table with two levels of column headers, or cells that span columns or rows, is outside this spec: split it.

A scrolling box must be reachable and operable by keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1) and its focus must be visible (2.4.7): TBL-22. It is a stop only while it scrolls, so short tables add nothing to the focus order.

Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10) exempts data tables from two-dimensional scrolling, and the table uses that exemption carefully: only its own box scrolls sideways, never the page (TBL-17, TBL-29), and a first column that stays in view is released on a narrow window (TBL-20).

Meaning never rests on color: stripes are an aid to the eye and say nothing; a status in a cell is a word, or a tag whose label says it. An empty cell is exposed as empty (TBL-14); where the absence itself is information ("not available", "none"), write it in the cell.

Contrast in the default system: cell text is on-surface and header text on-surface-variant, each held to 4.5:1 on every surface and container step by the token invariants, the stripe included. The lines are decorative: rows, headers and the region are exposed without them.
Alignment end for numbers is for sighted comparison only; it changes nothing that is exposed. Text is never justified and never centred except in a column the product sets to center.

A table with checkboxes stays a table (TBL-46). The grid pattern — one stop for the whole table, arrow keys from cell to cell — is for a sheet whose cells are edited or acted on; it takes over the keys a screen reader uses to read a table, it would replace the roles of the product's own table on the web, and it cannot work without script. The price of staying a table is one Tab stop for each row's checkbox, which pagination keeps to a page of rows.

Sorting is asked for and shown, never done, by the table (TBL-33, TBL-34): the header cell says the order (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2) and the mark repeats it to the eye without relying on color (1.4.1). One column is sorted at a time.

A chosen row is said by its checkbox, checked; the fill is the same fact for the eye and is not relied on (WCAG 1.4.1), which is also what is left in forced colors (TBL-54). In the default system the text of a chosen row is on-secondary-container on secondary-container, the pair a selected list item and a selected tree row are drawn in; the contrast of what a cell holds beside plain text on that fill is its own component's.

Status messages (WCAG 4.1.3): the table announces nothing itself (TBL-25) and gives the product one polite place to say what changed — rows found, rows chosen, loading and loaded (TBL-52). An Empty state in the empty slot that answers a search or a filter is live by its own spec.

While loading, the table is busy and placeholder rows are hidden (TBL-49, TBL-50), so that a person does not walk through rows of nothing. Do not take the rows a person was reading away for a spinner where they can stay.
Focus is never lost to a change of rows (TBL-25) and a focused control is never left under a part kept in view (TBL-36; WCAG 2.4.11).

web.name: tanrei-table

column.name: th
column.notes: A `<th scope="col">` in the `<thead>` row; its text is the header. `data-align="end"` and `data-wrap="false"` on that `<th>` reach every cell of the column: the element writes the positions of such columns on the wrapper (`data-columns-end`, `data-columns-center`, `data-columns-nowrap`) and one rule per position places the cells, so no cell is written to; without script, and from a Markdown renderer, the same attributes (or the renderer's own `align` attribute, where left and right are read as start and end) sit on each cell. A sortable column: the `<th>` holds the product's own `<button type="button">` (or, for a table ordered by the server, an `<a href>` to the same table in the other order) around the header's text, and carries `aria-sort="none"`, `"ascending"` or `"descending"`; the stylesheet draws the mark from that attribute, so the product writes no glyph. `data-value` on the `<th>` is the column's value.

row.name: tr
row.notes: A `<tr>`; a footer row is a `<tr>` inside `<tfoot>`. A row that can be chosen has `data-value` and a first cell `<td data-part="selection">` holding the product's checkbox — `<tanrei-checkbox label-hidden label="…">`, or a native `<input type="checkbox" aria-label="…">` that also works in a form without script; `selectLabel` is that checkbox's own name. `data-selected` on the `<tr>` draws the row as chosen; the element keeps it in step with the checkbox, and the stylesheet also reads a native checkbox that is checked, so a row is drawn chosen before and without script. A placeholder row is `<tr data-placeholder aria-hidden="true">`.

cell.name: td
cell.notes: A `<td>`, or a `<th scope="row">` for a row header; its children are the content.

web.notes:
Form: `` is a custom element with **no shadow root**, wrapped around a native `` that stays in the light DOM — `
………
…
`. The native table is never given another `display`, so its semantics, a crawler's reading, copy and paste as a table and a screen reader's table navigation are the browser's own. The wrapper is the scroll box (`display: block; overflow: auto; max-inline-size: 100%`; the product limits its height with `max-block-size`). Everything drawn comes from one stylesheet, `@tanrei/web/table.css`, whose selectors start at `tanrei-table` and are wrapped in `:where()`; it styles the page without script (an element that is not yet defined is still an element), and the element adopts the same sheet into the root it is connected to, so it also works inside another component's shadow root. Props are attributes of the wrapper: `density`, `separation`, `striped`, `row-headers`, `sticky-header`, `sticky-first-column`, `label`. `caption` is the native ``; the `caption` attribute is a convenience that writes one. `label` becomes `aria-label` on the table. Without script the table is fully drawn, scrolls in its box, and keeps its sticky parts; it lacks the two edge lines and, in a browser that does not focus scrollers by itself, the focus stop. Sticky parts are `position: sticky` on the cells (`inset-block-start: 0` on `thead th`, `inset-inline-start: 0` on the first cell of each row) with `border-collapse: separate` and the lines drawn as cell borders, because collapsed borders do not travel with a sticky cell. Inside `.tanrei-prose` the element is an island by its tag name (PRS-16). A cell that spans (`colspan`, `rowspan`) and a second header row keep working as HTML and are drawn with the same cell styles, but no fixture covers them. As built: the wrapper is a grid of one cell, not `display: block`, so that the two "there is more" lines are as tall as the table; the attributes the element writes are `data-more-start`, `data-more-end`, `data-more-above`, `data-first-column-released`, `data-columns` and the three positions above, and `data-separation` on the table; the region's `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` is copied from the table's own name where the product named it natively. **Sorting, selection, empty, loading and status: proposed form, for the platform's agent to settle.** Everything new is the product's own markup inside the same `

Neither checkbox is moved, wrapped or replaced. `sorted-ascending-label` and `sorted-descending-label` are accepted and not read: `aria-sort` is the browser's. Empty: the product writes `

swiftui.notes: Proposed spelling, for the platform's agent to settle. `TanreiTable(caption:, columns: [TanreiTableColumn], density:, …) { TanreiTableRow { TanreiTableCell("…"); TanreiTableCell { TanreiTag("Beta", size: .small) } } }`. Built on `Grid` and `GridRow` (columns sized from content, which is TBL-2) inside a `ScrollView` whose axes are the ones that overflow; a table of several hundred rows uses a `LazyVStack` of rows with column widths measured once from the header and a sample of rows. The platform's own `Table` is not used: it is a data table of its own look, with selection and sorting, and it collapses to its first column in a compact width. Sticky parts are pinned section headers (`pinnedViews`) for the header row and an overlaid first column whose offset follows the scroll. Accessibility: SwiftUI has no table container for custom views, so TBL-24's fallback applies — each row is an accessibility container in reading order, each cell's label is its column header followed by its content, header cells carry the header trait, and the scroll view is named by the caption. Sorting, selection, empty, loading and status: `TanreiTableColumn(header:, value:, isSortable:, sort:)`, `TanreiTable(selection: $values, onSort: { column, index, direction in … })` where `selection` is a binding to the set of chosen values, and rows take `value:`, `selectLabel:`, `isPlaceholder:`. A sortable header is a `Button` whose accessibility value is `sortedAscendingLabel` or `sortedDescendingLabel` (SwiftUI has no sort trait); the row's checkbox is `TanreiCheckbox`. The empty slot and the pagination slot are view builders (`empty:`, `pagination:`); the status text is posted as an announcement when it changes; `isLoading` sets nothing SwiftUI has a trait for, so placeholder rows are hidden and the status says it.

React Native has no table layout: rows are `View`s in a horizontal `ScrollView` (inside a vertical one, or a `FlatList` with `stickyHeaderIndices` for a long table), and column widths are measured in a first pass with `onLayout` and applied in a second, so the first frame of a large table is drawn after measuring.
